msg: crit. 2 at corner R=49.0 ohm / L=5.0 nH, best trimmer setting. Measured 39.99 dB.
crit. 2 at R=49.0 / 6.9 nH (architect's budget). Measured 40.13 dB.
crit. 2 at R=49.0 / 8.4 nH. Measured 40.23 dB.
crit. 2 at R=49.0 / 15.0 nH. Measured 40.97 dB - BETTER than the 5 nH corner, because below 50 ohm the series X pushes Reff = R + X^2/R back UP toward 50.
crit. 2 at R=50.0 / 5.0 nH. Measured 58.51 dB.
crit. 2 at the nominal corner R=50.0 / 6.9 nH. Measured 72.58 dB.
crit. 2 at R=50.0 / 8.4 nH. Measured 69.17 dB.
crit. 2 at R=50.0 / 15.0 nH. Measured 59.10 dB.
crit. 2 at R=51.0 / 5.0 nH. Measured 39.89 dB.
crit. 2 at R=51.0 / 6.9 nH (select-on-test upper limit + budget L). Measured 39.89 dB.
crit. 2 at R=51.0 / 8.4 nH. Measured 39.80 dB.
crit. 2 at R=51.0 / 15.0 nH. Measured 39.20 dB.
crit. 2 at the catalogue +5% corner R=52.5 / 5.0 nH. Measured 32.19 dB.
crit. 2 at R=52.5 / 6.9 nH. Measured 32.18 dB.
crit. 2 at R=52.5 / 8.4 nH. Measured 32.14 dB.
WORST OF ALL 16 CORNERS: R=52.5 / 15.0 nH. Measured 31.90 dB = 5.90 dB of margin over the 26 dB spec.
THE WRONG-VALUE CHECK, half 1: at the nominal resistance no inductance in the swept range gets anywhere near the spec. 5.0 nH -> 58.51 dB.
R=50.0 with 15.0 nH - 2.2x the architect's budget and 3x the 5 nH corner - still 59.10 dB, i.e. 33 dB clear of spec. Inductance is not the margin problem.

THE WRONG-VALUE CHECK, half 2: at the catalogue +5% resistance the best achievable RL is capped near 32 dB whatever the trimmer does, because a shunt susceptance cannot correct Re{Zin} (see reff_limit.cir). 32.19 dB.
R=52.5, 6.9 nH -> 32.18 dB, capped by resistance.
R=52.5, 8.4 nH -> 32.14 dB, capped by resistance.
R=52.5, 15.0 nH -> 31.90 dB. Tripling the inductance moved this corner by 0.28 dB; the 5% resistance error moved it by 40 dB.
the -2% select-on-test limit lands at 40.13 dB - 14 dB above spec and 8 dB above the +5% catalogue corner. This 7.7 dB step is what P1's select-on-test decision buys (decisions.md).
the +2% select-on-test limit lands at 39.89 dB, symmetric with the -2% limit.
RL(5.0 nH) - RL(15.0 nH) at R=49.0 = -0.97 dB. Tripling L moves RL by under 1 dB (and improves it below 50 ohm).
same spread at R=51.0 = +0.69 dB.
same spread at R=52.5 = +0.28 dB.

THE HEADLINE CONTRAST: at the budget inductance, going from R=50.0 to R=52.5 costs 40.40 dB of return loss. Compare dl_* above (< 1 dB for a 3x inductance change). The resistance tolerance IS the error budget.
the same resistance step still costs 27.20 dB at 15 nH.

best setting realizable in the swept 1-35 pF trimmer range. 1.000 pF = AT the low stop: the ideal null needs 0.78 pF, below any real trimmer, so this corner runs slightly over-corrected (harmless - RL is still 39.99 dB).
1.000 pF = at the low stop (ideal null 0.70 pF). All four L=5.0 nH corners bottom out; none of them is anywhere near failing spec.
1.459 pF - the setting the nominal board will actually be built to.
1.000 pF = at the low stop (ideal null 0.62 pF).
1.000 pF = at the low stop (ideal null 0.51 pF).
4.131 pF. Every one of the 16 best settings sits between 1.0 and 4.94 pF - the whole corner box lives in the bottom 12% of a 1-35 pF trimmer.
